description: Source recipes (spec/cli/sources.md, section 1). valid: readSourceRecipe on recipes/<name>.yaml given as file, returns recipe. broken: each starts from the text of from (a fixture in this folder), applies text (the whole text instead) or edits (each pair replaces the first occurrence of the first string by the second), is read as file recipes/<from>.yaml, and must fail with the message: exactly error, or, with errorStarts, one that begins so (the rest is the YAML reader's or the regular expression's reason). catalog: installedSourceRecipes on this folder lists these ids. origins: sourceOrigin (spec section 1, "A connection's recipe") for a connection, over the recipes of this folder (recipes: catalog) or no recipes (recipes: none); expected gives the recipe's id or null, the inputs and the problems.

database.description: The database whose tables are loaded, such as ERP

ask.who: Someone who can query the catalog views of the source database
ask.run:
SELECT c.TABLE_CATALOG AS table_catalog, c.TABLE_SCHEMA AS table_schema,
       c.TABLE_NAME AS table_name, c.COLUMN_NAME AS column_name,
       c.ORDINAL_POSITION AS ordinal_position, c.DATA_TYPE AS data_type,
       c.IS_NULLABLE AS is_nullable, k.ORDINAL_POSITION AS primary_key_position
FROM INFORMATION_SCHEMA.COLUMNS AS c
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT u.TABLE_CATALOG, u.TABLE_SCHEMA, u.TABLE_NAME, u.COLUMN_NAME, u.ORDINAL_POSITION
  FROM INFORMATION_SCHEMA.KEY_COLUMN_USAGE AS u
  JOIN INFORMATION_SCHEMA.TABLE_CONSTRAINTS AS t
    ON t.CONSTRAINT_NAME = u.CONSTRAINT_NAME AND t.TABLE_SCHEMA = u.TABLE_SCHEMA
  WHERE t.CONSTRAINT_TYPE = 'PRIMARY KEY'
) AS k ON k.TABLE_CATALOG = c.TABLE_CATALOG AND k.TABLE_SCHEMA = c.TABLE_SCHEMA
      AND k.TABLE_NAME = c.TABLE_NAME AND k.COLUMN_NAME = c.COLUMN_NAME
WHERE c.TABLE_SCHEMA IN ({schemas})
ask.how: Run the query in a SQL client and export the result as CSV with a header row.

broken.text:
id: sqlserver
title: SQL Server
kind: catalog
inputs:
  database: { description: "The database whose tables are loaded, such as ERP" }
ask:
  who: Someone who can query the catalog views of the source database
  access: VIEW DEFINITION on the database
  run: |
    SELECT c.TABLE_CATALOG AS table_catalog, c.TABLE_SCHEMA AS table_schema,
           c.TABLE_NAME AS table_name, c.COLUMN_NAME AS column_name,
           c.ORDINAL_POSITION AS ordinal_position, c.DATA_TYPE AS data_type,
           c.IS_NULLABLE AS is_nullable, k.ORDINAL_POSITION AS primary_key_position
    FROM INFORMATION_SCHEMA.COLUMNS AS c
    LEFT JOIN (
      SELECT u.TABLE_CATALOG, u.TABLE_SCHEMA, u.TABLE_NAME, u.COLUMN_NAME, u.ORDINAL_POSITION
      FROM INFORMATION_SCHEMA.KEY_COLUMN_USAGE AS u
      JOIN INFORMATION_SCHEMA.TABLE_CONSTRAINTS AS t
        ON t.CONSTRAINT_NAME = u.CONSTRAINT_NAME AND t.TABLE_SCHEMA = u.TABLE_SCHEMA
      WHERE t.CONSTRAINT_TYPE = 'PRIMARY KEY'
    ) AS k ON k.TABLE_CATALOG = c.TABLE_CATALOG AND k.TABLE_SCHEMA = c.TABLE_SCHEMA
          AND k.TABLE_NAME = c.TABLE_NAME AND k.COLUMN_NAME = c.COLUMN_NAME
    WHERE c.TABLE_SCHEMA IN ({schemas})
  save: sources/{connection}.catalog.csv
  how: Run the query in a SQL client and export the result as CSV with a header row.
read: columns
names: { parts: 3, caseSensitive: false }
types: nothing
sources:
  - { url: "https://example.com/sql-server/information-schema-columns", read: 2026-11-12 }
